page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the N2 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512 (including AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI), AES cryptography, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. This instance is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. It does not include any bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of cloud compute resources. In stress-ng testing, the single-core CPU performance scored 1399.29, while multi-core performance reached 1841.88. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block transfers measuring 13.72 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 11.78 GB/sec. Geekbench testing reflects similar constraints, yielding a single-core score of 1111.0 and a multi-core score of 1311.0. For specialized tasks, the instance achieved a static web serving throughput of 2.06 GB/sec and processed small 135M LLM inference prompts at 116.03 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point for dedicated CPU compute resources, but presents a clear trade-off in memory capacity. With only 2.0 GB of RAM, memory-intensive workloads will face severe bottlenecks. Consequently, this server is best suited for lightweight, CPU-bound workloads that require dedicated processing power but have minimal memory footprints, such as basic web serving, simple text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, or lightweight microservices.
